classification.difficultyReason: Find an unlabelled corner length using Pythagoras, subtract the triangular corner from a rectangle, then apply the painting rate.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows a metal plate that is to be painted.

spec.description: Unshaded five-sided plate with three right-angle marks, a full-width dimension arrow, and dashed red construction segments completing the missing upper-right corner. Ordinary source blue outlines are black under house style.
spec.mathematics: An enclosing 10 m by 8 m rectangle has a right-triangular corner removed. The corner has vertical leg 3 m and hypotenuse 5 m. Its unlabelled horizontal leg is 4 m; this value is used to construct the geometry but is not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens 10 m, 8 m, 5 m and 3 m are visible. No calculated length, area or cost is shown.

children.prompt: How much will it cost to paint the plate if paint costs $\$2.50$ per square metre?

inlines.text: Subtract the missing triangular corner from the rectangle, then multiply the remaining area by the cost per square metre.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras, the horizontal length of the removed corner is
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Corner length}&=\sqrt{5^2-3^2}\\
\text{Corner length}&=4\text{ m}.
\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Corner area}&=\tfrac12\times4\times3\\
\text{Corner area}&=6\text{ m}^2\\
\text{Plate area}&=10\times8-6\\
\text{Plate area}&=74\text{ m}^2\\
\text{Cost}&=74\times\$2.50\\
\text{Cost}&=\$185.
\end{align*}$$
